cases.sentence: ___, сидевшая прежде с ma tante, торопливо встала и догнала князя Василья в передней.
cases.explain: «Пожилая дама» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Anna Pávlovna smiled and promised to take Pierre in hand. She knew his father to be a connection of Prince Vasíli’s. The elderly lady who had been sitting with the old aunt rose hurriedly and overtook Prince Vasíli in the anteroom. All the affectation of interest she had assumed had left her kindly and tear-worn face and it now expressed only anxiety and fear.

cases.sentence: (Она выговаривала имя Борис с ___ на о).
cases.explain: «особенным ударением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “How about my son Borís, Prince?” said she, hurrying after him into the anteroom. “I can’t remain any longer in Petersburg. Tell me what news I may take back to my poor boy.”

cases.sentence: Скажите, какие известия я могу привезти моему ___?
cases.explain: «бедному мальчику» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.

cases.sentence: ___ носила имя княгини Друбецкой, одной из лучших фамилий России, но она была бедна, давно вышла из света и утратила прежние связи.
cases.explain: «Пожилая дама» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The elderly lady was a Princess Drubetskáya, belonging to one of the best families in Russia, but she was poor, and having long been out of society had lost her former influential connections. She had now come to Petersburg to procure an appointment in the Guards for her only son. It was, in fact, solely to meet Prince Vasíli that she had obtained an invitation to Anna Pávlovna’s reception and had sat listening to the vicomte’s story. Prince Vasíli’s words frightened her, an embittered look clouded her once handsome face, but only for a moment; then she smiled again and clutched Prince Vasíli’s arm more tightly.

cases.sentence: — сказала, повернув свою красивую голову на ___, княжна Элен, ожидавшая у двери.
cases.explain: «античных плечах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Papa, we shall be late,” said Princess Elèn, turning her beautiful head and looking over her classically molded shoulder as she stood waiting by the door.

cases.sentence: В деле княгини Друбецкой он почувствовал, однако, после ее ___, что-то в роде укора совести.
cases.explain: «нового призыва» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Influence in society, however, is a capital which has to be economized if it is to last. Prince Vasíli knew this, and having once realized that if he asked on behalf of all who begged of him, he would soon be unable to ask for himself, he became chary of using his influence. But in Princess Drubetskáya’s case he felt, after her second appeal, something like qualms of conscience. She had reminded him of what was quite true; he had been indebted to her father for the first steps in his career. Moreover, he could see by her manners that she was one of those women—mostly mothers—who, having once made up their minds, will not rest until they have gained their end, and are prepared if necessary to go on insisting day after day and hour after hour, and even to make scenes. This last consideration moved him.

cases.sentence: Он мне сам говорил, что все ___ сговорились отдать ему всех своих детей в адъютанты.
cases.explain: «московские барыни» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No, I won’t promise that. You don’t know how Kutúzov is pestered since his appointment as Commander in Chief. He told me himself that all the Moscow ladies have conspired to give him all their sons as adjutants.”

cases.sentence: Князь Ипполит, долго смотревший в лорнет на виконта, вдруг при этих словах повернулся всем телом к ___ и, попросив у нее иголку, стал показывать ей, рисуя иголкой на столе, герб Конде.
cases.explain: «маленькой княгине» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: And sighing disdainfully, he again changed his position. Prince Ippolit, who had been gazing at the vicomte for some time through his lorgnette, suddenly turned completely round toward the little princess, and having asked for a needle began tracing the Condé coat of arms on the table. He explained this to her with as much gravity as if she had asked him to do it.

cases.sentence: Он растолковывал ей этот герб с таким ___, как будто княгиня просила его об этом.

cases.sentence: — Император Александр, — сказала она с грустью, сопутствовавшею всегда ее речам об императорской фамилии, — объявил, что он предоставит ___ выбрать образ правления.
cases.explain: «самим французам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “The Emperor Alexander,” said she, with the melancholy which always accompanied any reference of hers to the Imperial family, “has declared that he will leave it to the French people themselves to choose their own form of government; and I believe that once free from the usurper, the whole nation will certainly throw itself into the arms of its rightful king,” she concluded, trying to be amiable to the royalist emigrant.

cases.sentence: И я думаю, нет сомнения, что вся нация, освободившись от узурпатора, бросится в руки ___, — сказала Анна Павловна, стараясь быть любезной с эмигрантом и роялистом.
cases.explain: «законного короля» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The Emperor Alexander,” said she, with the melancholy which always accompanied any reference of hers to the Imperial family, “has declared that he will leave it to the French people themselves to choose their own form of government; and I believe that once free from the usurper, the whole nation will certainly throw itself into the arms of its rightful king,” she concluded, trying to be amiable to the royalist emigrant.

cases.sentence: — ___ проговорила Анна Павловна.
cases.explain: «страшным шопотом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Dieu! Mon Dieu!” muttered Anna Pávlovna in a terrified whisper.

cases.sentence: — Comment, М. Pierre, vous trouvez que l’assassinat est grandeur d’âme,[84] Как, мсье Пьер, вы видите в убийстве величие души, — сказала ___, улыбаясь и придвигая к себе работу.
cases.explain: «маленькая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What, Monsieur Pierre … Do you consider that assassination shows greatness of soul?” said the little princess, smiling and drawing her work nearer to her.

cases.sentence: — Да, ежели бы он, взяв власть, не пользуясь ею для убийства, отдал бы ее ___, — сказал виконт, — тогда бы я назвал его великим человеком.
cases.explain: «законному королю» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Yes, if having obtained power, without availing himself of it to commit murder he had restored it to the rightful king, I should have called him a great man,” remarked the vicomte.

cases.sentence: — Да, ежели бы он, взяв власть, не пользуясь ею для убийства, отдал бы ее законному королю, — сказал виконт, — тогда бы я назвал его ___.

cases.sentence: Революция была ___, — продолжал мсье Пьер, выказывая этим отчаянным и вызывающим вводным предложением свою великую молодость и желание всё поскорее высказать.
cases.explain: «великое дело» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “He could not do that. The people only gave him power that he might rid them of the Bourbons and because they saw that he was a great man. The Revolution was a grand thing!” continued Monsieur Pierre, betraying by this desperate and provocative proposition his extreme youth and his wish to express all that was in his mind.

cases.sentence: Революция была великое дело, — продолжал мсье Пьер, выказывая этим отчаянным и вызывающим ___ свою великую молодость и желание всё поскорее высказать.

The Revolution was a grand thing!” continued Monsieur Pierre, betraying by this desperate and provocative proposition his extreme youth and his wish to express all that was in his mind.

cases.explain: «Общественный договор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Rousseau’s Contrat Social,” said the vicomte with a tolerant smile.

cases.sentence: — Свобода и равенство, — презрительно сказал виконт, как будто решившийся, наконец, серьезно доказать этому юноше всю глупость его речей, — всё ___, которые уже давно компрометировались.
cases.explain: «громкие слова» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Liberty and equality,” said the vicomte contemptuously, as if at last deciding seriously to prove to this youth how foolish his words were, “high-sounding words which have long been discredited. Who does not love liberty and equality? Even our Saviour preached liberty and equality. Have people since the Revolution become happier? On the contrary. We wanted liberty, but Bonaparte has destroyed it.”

cases.sentence: Разве это не обман? C’est un escamotage, qui ne ressemble nullement à la manière d’agir d’un grand homme.[88] Это шулерство, вовсе не похожее на образ действий ___.
cases.explain: «великого человека» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I should like,” said the vicomte, “to ask how monsieur explains the 18th Brumaire; was not that an imposture? It was a swindle, and not at all like the conduct of a great man!”

cases.translation: “And the prisoners he killed in Africa? That was horrible!” said the little princess, shrugging her shoulders.

cases.sentence: Улыбка у него была не такая, как у ___, сливающаяся с неулыбкой.

cases.translation: Pierre, not knowing whom to answer, looked at them all and smiled. His smile was unlike the half-smile of other people. When he smiled, his grave, even rather gloomy, look was instantaneously replaced by another—a childlike, kindly, even rather silly look, which seemed to ask forgiveness.

cases.sentence: — Притом надо в поступках ___ различать поступки частного лица, полководца или императора.

cases.translation: “How do you expect him to answer you all at once?” said Prince Andréy. “Besides, in the actions of a statesman one has to distinguish between his acts as a private person, as a general, and as an emperor. So it seems to me.”

cases.sentence: — Нельзя не сознаться, — продолжал князь Андрей, — Наполеон как человек велик на Аркольском мосту, в госпитале в Яффе, где он чумным подает руку, но... но есть ___, которые трудно оправдать.

cases.translation: “One must admit,” continued Prince Andréy, “that Napoleon as a man was great on the bridge of Arcola, and in the hospital at Jaffa where he gave his hand to the plague-stricken; but … but there are other acts which it is difficult to justify.”

cases.sentence: Однако многие, и в том числе ___ и Анна Павловна, улыбнулись.
cases.explain: «пожилая дама» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Here Prince Ippolit spluttered and burst out laughing long before his audience, which produced an effect unfavorable to the narrator. Several persons, among them the elderly lady and Anna Pávlovna, did however smile.

cases.translation: “She went. Suddenly there was a great wind. The girl lost her hat and her long hair came down. …” Here he could contain himself no longer and went on, between gasps of laughter: “And the whole world knew. …”
